note: As of the Tue 17 Nov US close / pre-Asia-open Wed 18 Nov (SGX 09:00, HKEX 09:30 SGT not yet open at run time). Several items are genuinely fresh (16-17 Nov); overnight-Asia-specific news had not yet broken at 07:02 SGT, which is expected rather than a gap.

items.headline: Fed's Waller flags a possible 50bp December hike; Dec 9 FOMC odds harden to ~95-98% for at least 25bp
items.summary: Fed Governor Waller said in London he'd back a 50bp December hike if core CPI prints 0.3%+ again, warning a mere 25bp move risks the Fed's credibility; Dallas Fed's Lorie Logan separately backed at least two more hikes. Odds-market pricing for a 25bp hike at the Dec 9 FOMC has moved from roughly 68% hold-odds in August to ~95-98% hike-odds now, a dramatic reversal from cut-leaning pricing just weeks ago.
items.actionable: This is the single biggest threat to the levered silver/miners book -- a hawkish surprise combined with dollar strength would pressure silver just as margin sensitivity on the loan is highest; the Oct FOMC minutes drop 19 Nov and are a must-watch before Asia opens Thursday.

items.headline: Nvidia crushes Q3 estimates, guides Q4 to ~$130bn -- first report without Jensen Huang
items.summary: Revenue hit $115.8bn (+103% YoY, beat the $109bn consensus), Data Center revenue $107.6bn, non-GAAP EPS $2.68 (beat $2.48 est.), a $150bn buyback was announced, and Q4 guidance of ~$130bn topped the ~$125bn Street estimate. Shares rose after hours despite the stock having slid into the print amid the broader two-day risk-off tape and Huang's Nov 12 resignation.
items.actionable: Confirms AI-capex demand is intact -- a bullish offset to the chip-export-control/Huang-scandal overhang that should support sentiment in SMIC/Tencent at Wednesday's HK open, though NVDA is not a direct holding.

items.headline: US tightens AI-chip export controls, closing the 'remote access' loophole -- hits right before Trump-Xi summit
items.summary: Commerce's BIS issued an interim rule requiring licenses for AI chips/servers going to any data center that might provide compute to China, and extended licensing requirements to Singapore, Malaysia, Thailand, Indonesia and Brazil as 'diversion risk' jurisdictions. It lands the same week Trump travels to China for APEC and amid fallout from the Huang scandal's national-security angle.
items.actionable: This directly triggered Tuesday's SMIC/HK-chip rotation (below); watch whether Singapore's new inclusion on the 'diversion risk' list creates any secondary friction for SGX-listed tech/logistics names.

items.headline: SMIC surges 6.8% Tuesday on chip self-sufficiency rotation + strong Q3; Tencent falls 3.7%
items.summary: SMIC jumped as the new US export curbs triggered a rotation into domestic Chinese foundries even as the Hang Seng Tech Index fell broadly, compounding a strong Q3 (revenue +33.9% YoY, net profit +123.4%, gross margin 29.9%). Tencent fell 3.69% the same session even as Southbound Stock Connect was a net buyer of both names Tuesday (Tencent +HK$1.60bn, SMIC +HK$1.13bn) while selling Alibaba (-HK$1.56bn).
items.actionable: A genuine idiosyncratic positive for the SMIC position even as Tencent sold off on the same news -- Tencent reports its own Q3 results 18 Nov, the next read-through for the HK-tech sleeve.

items.headline: Jensen Huang says he'd return as CEO 'if asked' -- board says no, search firm hired
items.summary: In his first public remarks since the Nov 12 resignation, Huang said 'I own my mistakes completely' but added he'd be honored to return if the board asked. CNBC reports the board has hired outside counsel and begun selecting a search firm, and is not currently considering reinstating him; an online petition for his return has 180,000+ signatures and public backing from Elon Musk.
items.actionable: The scandal's national-security angle is part of the backdrop for the new export curbs above -- watch for any read-through to US-China tech diplomacy at this week's APEC summit.

items.headline: Trump-Xi-Putin trilateral summit at APEC, Shenzhen -- unprecedented three-way meeting
items.summary: Trump, Xi and Putin are holding a first-ever three-way summit on the sidelines of APEC in Shenzhen, China's tech hub, with a Trump-Xi bilateral followed by the trilateral; the agenda reportedly includes the Iran war and denuclearization alongside trade.
items.actionable: The single biggest geopolitical wildcard overhanging the HK-tech and rare-earth books this week -- any trade/tariff signal out of Shenzhen over the next 48 hours could move Tencent/SMIC and rare-earth truce status sharply either way; conviction is low given the summit is happening as this is written.

items.headline: Gold near 14-month lows, silver diverging higher -- the metals/margin picture
items.summary: Gold slipped to ~$3,852/oz (lowest since Sep 2025) on a firmer dollar and hike repricing, while silver bucked the trend, up ~0.6-1.1% to $42.64 (SLV) / $47.29 (futures). Since the Nov 10 hot-CPI print, gold has shed ~$300 and silver ~$6, but managed-money futures positioning has fallen more than ETF holdings, suggesting leveraged longs -- not physical holders -- are driving the selloff.
items.actionable: The gold/silver divergence is consistent with the thesis that miners (GDX/SILJ/SLVP) are more resilient than the broad tape right now, but a confirmed Fed hike would hit the weaker (gold) leg first and test the gold-silver ratio -- worth checking loan margin buffers against a silver pullback scenario, not a gold one.

items.headline: China extends rare-earth export-control suspension to 10 Jan 2027 -- but dysprosium/terbium/yttrium curbs stay
items.summary: MOFCOM and Customs confirmed the suspension of the more severe Oct 9 controls (the 0.1% de minimis rule plus license requirements on five additional elements) was extended from its scheduled 10 Nov lapse through 10 Jan 2027. The pause does not cover controls already in place on dysprosium, terbium and yttrium, which remain elevated in price.
items.actionable: The truce extension removes a near-term tail risk for the rare-earth watchlist, but it's a temporary reprieve expiring right before Chinese New Year, and leaves the dysprosium/terbium squeeze intact -- a tailwind specifically for Lynas/Energy Fuels over light-REE names.

items.headline: MP Materials Q3: revenue +176%, DoD price-floor deal -- but rare-earth basket sold off into Trump-Xi
items.summary: MP Materials posted Q3 revenue of $147.7M (+176% YoY) with NdPr production +41% to 1,018 metric tons and adj. EBITDA of $41.1M, underpinned by its 10-year 100% DoD magnet-offtake deal and $110/kg NdPr price floor. Despite the strong print, the rare-earth-equity basket sold off Tuesday ahead of the Trump-Xi meeting -- USA Rare Earth -7%, Critical Metals -5%, MP itself -3.4% -- as traders de-risked pending summit headlines.
items.actionable: MP's fundamentals and DoD backstop look intact and arguably strengthening, so Tuesday's dip reads as summit-related de-risking rather than a thesis break -- a reasonable add-on-weakness candidate for the watchlist once Shenzhen headlines clarify.

items.headline: Lynas falls 7-8% Tuesday -- broad ASX miner selloff, not stock-specific news
items.summary: Lynas fell alongside Mineral Resources and PLS Group as the ASX 200 slumped, dragged by the overnight Wall Street tech selloff plus weaker industrial/precious-metals prices broadly -- no Lynas-specific negative catalyst (no earnings, no guidance cut) behind the drop. This continues a stock already down ~42% over six months on prior operational/consensus-miss news (the Meteoric Resources acquisition dilution, August's profit miss).
items.actionable: Because this looks purely sentiment/beta-driven rather than fundamental, it's a candidate to monitor for a bounce if Wednesday's Asia tape stabilizes -- but the stock remains structurally weak independent of Tuesday's move, so don't mistake 'no new bad news' for 'thesis intact'.

items.headline: SGX banks diverge: OCBC beats and raises guidance, DBS/UOB miss; CDL flags weaker H2
items.summary: OCBC was the only one of the three banks to beat Q3 estimates (net profit +3% YoY to S$2.04bn) and raised 2026 loan-growth guidance; DBS posted a 5% profit decline (9M profit still a record S$8.82bn) and UOB also missed. City Developments warned H2 2026 will be 'significantly weaker' than H1 due to delayed asset-recycling deals, KRW/SGD FX losses and potential portfolio impairments; Keppel REIT separately agreed to buy 51% of Keppel South Central (9M NPI +12.7%).
items.actionable: OCBC's beat-and-raise is a relative-strength signal within the SGX bank exposure versus DBS/UOB; the CDL profit warning (impairment risk flagged explicitly) is the one SGX developer name needing closer monitoring given it's company-specific, not just beta.

items.headline: Bitcoin near four-month low; ETF outflows top $1bn for a second straight week
items.summary: Bitcoin fell as low as ~$62,612 on Sunday before stabilizing near $64,792 Tuesday, its weakest level since July, as the 10-year yield above 5% and Fed hike repricing drove crypto fund outflows of $1.07bn -- the second consecutive week above $1bn. Wintermute flagged risk of a slide into the $50,000s; MSCI separately confirmed it will drop Strategy (MSTR) from its indexes.
items.actionable: A clean, independent confirmation that the same rate/dollar forces pressuring gold are also hitting the most liquid 24/7 risk-sentiment barometer -- crypto's synchronized weakness with equities reinforces that Dec-hike repricing, not an idiosyncratic event, is the dominant cross-asset driver right now.

items.headline: Oil slips as IEA flags Q4 global surplus; Brent near $93
items.summary: WTI held near $85.61 (-0.13%) and Brent futures ticked up slightly to $93.07 as expectations of a global supply surplus outweighed lingering Middle East infrastructure/shipping concerns; the IEA said the oil market should return to surplus in Q4 as Middle East exports recover faster than demand.
items.actionable: No direct portfolio holding here, but a soft oil price is modestly disinflationary and could, at the margin, cut against the hawkish-Fed narrative above if it persists -- worth tracking as a secondary input to the Dec 9 rate call, not an immediate trade.
